lanes.summary: I reviewed points 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 from the provided inline diffs, and did not read the external patch file. I found real defects in all six points: [P1] misses method calls in `is_dynamic_exec`; [P2] misses array expansions for other functions and suffers from newline stripping on empty items; [P3] mishandles `set`/`shopt` as non-code, escalating next-line suppressions to file-level; [P4] hides DET005 behind DET002 due to class outranking; [P5] falsely accepts `break` inside same-line subshells/functions due to byte-order regex logic ignoring lexical scope; and [P6] misses command substitutions embedded inside braced variable expansions because the new lexer skips the entire brace body. I did not review points 7, 8, 9, or 10.

findings.claim: [P1] `is_dynamic_exec` does not match `Expr::MethodCall`, so if `exec()` or `capture()` are called as methods (e.g. `dynamic.exec()`), `dynamic` remains false and all literals bypass the substitution check.
findings.fix: Add a match arm in `is_dynamic_exec` for `Expr::MethodCall` checking the method name against `EXEC_FNS`.

findings.claim: [P2] `convert_array_stdlib_call` only intercepts `array_len` and `array_join`. If a local array is passed to any other stdlib or user-defined function, it falls back to `convert_expr_to_value`, which emits the unset scalar `"$name"`. Furthermore, for empty arrays or arrays with empty trailing strings, `$(printf '%s\n' ...)` strips trailing newlines, corrupting the length.
findings.fix: Move array resolution into `convert_expr_to_value` to cover all usages, and avoid `$( )` newline-stripping by appending a non-empty sentinel before command substitution, or using `set --` / positional parameters instead of newline-joined strings.

findings.claim: [P3] `is_code_line` ignores `set` and `shopt` commands, causing a `# shellcheck disable=` directive placed after them to still see `seen_code == false`. This erroneously escalates a next-line shellcheck suppression into a file-level suppression.
findings.fix: Remove `&& !trimmed.starts_with("set ") && !trimmed.starts_with("shopt ")` from `is_code_line`, as these are real commands and disqualify subsequent directives from being file-level in shellcheck.

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule implements mutual exclusion by having `SinkClass::Reproducible` outrank `SinkClass::Conditional`. A timestamp reaching both a branch condition and a build artifact is only flagged by DET002, hiding the DET005 time-dependent control flow defect.
findings.fix: Instead of outranking, allow a `TimestampUse` to carry a bitmask of sink types so DET002 and DET005 can both independently fire if their respective hazard is present.

findings.claim: [P5] PMAT-244's byte-order fix accepts a `break` physically located between `do` and `done` on a single line, but this ignores lexical scoping. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` or function `f() { break; }` on that same line is now falsely accepted (missed), whereas the old buggy line-level sum accidentally caught it by dropping depth to 0 via `done` before checking.
findings.fix: `SC2105` must track subshell/function depths, or use a proper AST instead of regex byte-order, to ensure `break` actually belongs to the loop and not an opaque inner scope.

findings.claim: [P6] The `shell_words` refactor changes the SC2046 verdict for a command substitution inside a braced variable expansion (e.g., `echo ${var:-$(date)}`). The old private scanner scanned blindly and found the `$(`, but `shell_words::WordLexer` consumes the entire `${...}` block and skips its body, missing the substitution inside.
findings.fix: If `shell_words` now handles this, it must recursively scan the inside of braced expansions for command substitutions, or SC2046 must keep its private scanner for the raw text.

lanes.summary: Reviewed points 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9 using the inline text only. Points 3 and 7 are sound. Found defects in 4, 5, 8, and 9: the no-double-report rule masks DET005 behind Unknown sinks (P4); SC2105's regex-based loop depth ignores shell grammar boundaries like subshells and case arms (P5); the publish script trusts a caller-supplied worktree without verifying it matches the tag (P8); and the CI wait step polls the immediately-consistent Web API instead of the asynchronous cargo index (P9).

findings.claim: [P3] no defect found: checked suppression handling (file-level, next-line, mixed directives, seen_code tracking) and it correctly isolates SC codes for shellcheck directives while reporting native codes.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: [P7] no defect found: checked dogfood scripts (contracts.sh, corpus.sh, docs.sh) and found no path that prints PASS without measuring. Each validates the output of the commands and handles empty results correctly.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule introduces a false negative: if a timestamp reaches both a branch condition (Conditional sink) and an unrecognised command (Unknown sink), the `Unknown` classification outranks `Conditional`. Only DET002 is reported, masking the time-dependent control flow defect (DET005). Suppressing DET002 then silently ignores the branch condition hazard.
findings.fix: Track Conditional and Reproducible/Unknown sinks as independent boolean flags in FlowState so both rules can evaluate and be suppressed independently.

findings.claim: [P5] SC2105 purely lexical loop_depth tracking misses illegal breaks because it ignores shell grammar boundaries. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` is completely missed, as is a `break` outside a loop if a preceding case arm or inline comment contains a loop keyword (e.g. `do)`), which falsely increments the depth counter.
findings.fix: Strip comments and strings before regex matching, or rely on AST/IR loop structures instead of physical line text.

findings.claim: [P8] When `--worktree DIR` is provided, the script never checks if `DIR` is actually checked out to `$TAG`. It will silently publish whatever code is checked out in `DIR` while incorrectly printing the version of `$TAG` read from the ambient repository.
findings.fix: Add `[ "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse "$TAG^{commit}")" ]` to ensure the caller's worktree matches the tag.

findings.claim: [P9] The wait step incorrectly polls the crates.io Web API (`/api/v1/crates/...`), which updates immediately upon publish. Cargo resolves dependencies against the registry index (sparse or git), which updates asynchronously. Polling the Web API will return 200 before the index has actually caught up, failing to prevent the `cargo package` race.
findings.fix: Poll the sparse registry index directly (e.g., `https://index.crates.io/ba/sh/bashrs-oracle`) or use `cargo search bashrs-oracle` to verify the index.

I found real defects in all six points: [P1] misses method calls in `is_dynamic_exec`; [P2] misses array expansions for other functions and suffers from newline stripping on empty items; [P3] mishandles `set`/`shopt` as non-code, escalating next-line suppressions to file-level; [P4] hides DET005 behind DET002 due to class outranking; [P5] falsely accepts `break` inside same-line subshells/functions due to byte-order regex logic ignoring lexical scope; and [P6] misses command substitutions embedded inside braced variable expansions because the new lexer skips the entire brace body. I did not review points 7, 8, 9, or 10.

findings.claim: [P1] `is_dynamic_exec` does not match `Expr::MethodCall`, so if `exec()` or `capture()` are called as methods (e.g. `dynamic.exec()`), `dynamic` remains false and all literals bypass the substitution check.
findings.fix: Add a match arm in `is_dynamic_exec` for `Expr::MethodCall` checking the method name against `EXEC_FNS`.

findings.claim: [P2] `convert_array_stdlib_call` only intercepts `array_len` and `array_join`. If a local array is passed to any other stdlib or user-defined function, it falls back to `convert_expr_to_value`, which emits the unset scalar `"$name"`. Furthermore, for empty arrays or arrays with empty trailing strings, `$(printf '%s\n' ...)` strips trailing newlines, corrupting the length.
findings.fix: Move array resolution into `convert_expr_to_value` to cover all usages, and avoid `$( )` newline-stripping by appending a non-empty sentinel before command substitution, or using `set --` / positional parameters instead of newline-joined strings.

findings.claim: [P3] `is_code_line` ignores `set` and `shopt` commands, causing a `# shellcheck disable=` directive placed after them to still see `seen_code == false`. This erroneously escalates a next-line shellcheck suppression into a file-level suppression.
findings.fix: Remove `&& !trimmed.starts_with("set ") && !trimmed.starts_with("shopt ")` from `is_code_line`, as these are real commands and disqualify subsequent directives from being file-level in shellcheck.

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule implements mutual exclusion by having `SinkClass::Reproducible` outrank `SinkClass::Conditional`. A timestamp reaching both a branch condition and a build artifact is only flagged by DET002, hiding the DET005 time-dependent control flow defect.
findings.fix: Instead of outranking, allow a `TimestampUse` to carry a bitmask of sink types so DET002 and DET005 can both independently fire if their respective hazard is present.

findings.claim: [P5] PMAT-244's byte-order fix accepts a `break` physically located between `do` and `done` on a single line, but this ignores lexical scoping. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` or function `f() { break; }` on that same line is now falsely accepted (missed), whereas the old buggy line-level sum accidentally caught it by dropping depth to 0 via `done` before checking.
findings.fix: `SC2105` must track subshell/function depths, or use a proper AST instead of regex byte-order, to ensure `break` actually belongs to the loop and not an opaque inner scope.

findings.claim: [P6] The `shell_words` refactor changes the SC2046 verdict for a command substitution inside a braced variable expansion (e.g., `echo ${var:-$(date)}`). The old private scanner scanned blindly and found the `$(`, but `shell_words::WordLexer` consumes the entire `${...}` block and skips its body, missing the substitution inside.
findings.fix: If `shell_words` now handles this, it must recursively scan the inside of braced expansions for command substitutions, or SC2046 must keep its private scanner for the raw text.

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule introduces a false negative: if a timestamp reaches both a branch condition (Conditional sink) and an unrecognised command (Unknown sink), the `Unknown` classification outranks `Conditional`. Only DET002 is reported, masking the time-dependent control flow defect (DET005). Suppressing DET002 then silently ignores the branch condition hazard.
findings.fix: Track Conditional and Reproducible/Unknown sinks as independent boolean flags in FlowState so both rules can evaluate and be suppressed independently.

findings.claim: [P5] SC2105 purely lexical loop_depth tracking misses illegal breaks because it ignores shell grammar boundaries. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` is completely missed, as is a `break` outside a loop if a preceding case arm or inline comment contains a loop keyword (e.g. `do)`), which falsely increments the depth counter.
findings.fix: Strip comments and strings before regex matching, or rely on AST/IR loop structures instead of physical line text.

findings.claim: [P8] When `--worktree DIR` is provided, the script never checks if `DIR` is actually checked out to `$TAG`. It will silently publish whatever code is checked out in `DIR` while incorrectly printing the version of `$TAG` read from the ambient repository.
findings.fix: Add `[ "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse "$TAG^{commit}")" ]` to ensure the caller's worktree matches the tag.

findings.claim: [P9] The wait step incorrectly polls the crates.io Web API (`/api/v1/crates/...`), which updates immediately upon publish. Cargo resolves dependencies against the registry index (sparse or git), which updates asynchronously. Polling the Web API will return 200 before the index has actually caught up, failing to prevent the `cargo package` race.
findings.fix: Poll the sparse registry index directly (e.g., `https://index.crates.io/ba/sh/bashrs-oracle`) or use `cargo search bashrs-oracle` to verify the index.

I found real defects in all six points: [P1] misses method calls in `is_dynamic_exec`; [P2] misses array expansions for other functions and suffers from newline stripping on empty items; [P3] mishandles `set`/`shopt` as non-code, escalating next-line suppressions to file-level; [P4] hides DET005 behind DET002 due to class outranking; [P5] falsely accepts `break` inside same-line subshells/functions due to byte-order regex logic ignoring lexical scope; and [P6] misses command substitutions embedded inside braced variable expansions because the new lexer skips the entire brace body. I did not review points 7, 8, 9, or 10.

findings.claim: [P1] `is_dynamic_exec` does not match `Expr::MethodCall`, so if `exec()` or `capture()` are called as methods (e.g. `dynamic.exec()`), `dynamic` remains false and all literals bypass the substitution check.
findings.fix: Add a match arm in `is_dynamic_exec` for `Expr::MethodCall` checking the method name against `EXEC_FNS`.

findings.claim: [P2] `convert_array_stdlib_call` only intercepts `array_len` and `array_join`. If a local array is passed to any other stdlib or user-defined function, it falls back to `convert_expr_to_value`, which emits the unset scalar `"$name"`. Furthermore, for empty arrays or arrays with empty trailing strings, `$(printf '%s\n' ...)` strips trailing newlines, corrupting the length.
findings.fix: Move array resolution into `convert_expr_to_value` to cover all usages, and avoid `$( )` newline-stripping by appending a non-empty sentinel before command substitution, or using `set --` / positional parameters instead of newline-joined strings.

findings.claim: [P3] `is_code_line` ignores `set` and `shopt` commands, causing a `# shellcheck disable=` directive placed after them to still see `seen_code == false`. This erroneously escalates a next-line shellcheck suppression into a file-level suppression.
findings.fix: Remove `&& !trimmed.starts_with("set ") && !trimmed.starts_with("shopt ")` from `is_code_line`, as these are real commands and disqualify subsequent directives from being file-level in shellcheck.

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule implements mutual exclusion by having `SinkClass::Reproducible` outrank `SinkClass::Conditional`. A timestamp reaching both a branch condition and a build artifact is only flagged by DET002, hiding the DET005 time-dependent control flow defect.
findings.fix: Instead of outranking, allow a `TimestampUse` to carry a bitmask of sink types so DET002 and DET005 can both independently fire if their respective hazard is present.

findings.claim: [P5] PMAT-244's byte-order fix accepts a `break` physically located between `do` and `done` on a single line, but this ignores lexical scoping. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` or function `f() { break; }` on that same line is now falsely accepted (missed), whereas the old buggy line-level sum accidentally caught it by dropping depth to 0 via `done` before checking.
findings.fix: `SC2105` must track subshell/function depths, or use a proper AST instead of regex byte-order, to ensure `break` actually belongs to the loop and not an opaque inner scope.

findings.claim: [P6] The `shell_words` refactor changes the SC2046 verdict for a command substitution inside a braced variable expansion (e.g., `echo ${var:-$(date)}`). The old private scanner scanned blindly and found the `$(`, but `shell_words::WordLexer` consumes the entire `${...}` block and skips its body, missing the substitution inside.
findings.fix: If `shell_words` now handles this, it must recursively scan the inside of braced expansions for command substitutions, or SC2046 must keep its private scanner for the raw text.

dissent.summary: Reviewed points 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9 using the inline text only. Points 3 and 7 are sound. Found defects in 4, 5, 8, and 9: the no-double-report rule masks DET005 behind Unknown sinks (P4); SC2105's regex-based loop depth ignores shell grammar boundaries like subshells and case arms (P5); the publish script trusts a caller-supplied worktree without verifying it matches the tag (P8); and the CI wait step polls the immediately-consistent Web API instead of the asynchronous cargo index (P9).

findings.claim: [P3] no defect found: checked suppression handling (file-level, next-line, mixed directives, seen_code tracking) and it correctly isolates SC codes for shellcheck directives while reporting native codes.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: [P7] no defect found: checked dogfood scripts (contracts.sh, corpus.sh, docs.sh) and found no path that prints PASS without measuring. Each validates the output of the commands and handles empty results correctly.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: [P4] The no-double-report rule introduces a false negative: if a timestamp reaches both a branch condition (Conditional sink) and an unrecognised command (Unknown sink), the `Unknown` classification outranks `Conditional`. Only DET002 is reported, masking the time-dependent control flow defect (DET005). Suppressing DET002 then silently ignores the branch condition hazard.
findings.fix: Track Conditional and Reproducible/Unknown sinks as independent boolean flags in FlowState so both rules can evaluate and be suppressed independently.

findings.claim: [P5] SC2105 purely lexical loop_depth tracking misses illegal breaks because it ignores shell grammar boundaries. A `break` inside a subshell `( break )` is completely missed, as is a `break` outside a loop if a preceding case arm or inline comment contains a loop keyword (e.g. `do)`), which falsely increments the depth counter.
findings.fix: Strip comments and strings before regex matching, or rely on AST/IR loop structures instead of physical line text.

findings.claim: [P8] When `--worktree DIR` is provided, the script never checks if `DIR` is actually checked out to `$TAG`. It will silently publish whatever code is checked out in `DIR` while incorrectly printing the version of `$TAG` read from the ambient repository.
findings.fix: Add `[ "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse "$TAG^{commit}")" ]` to ensure the caller's worktree matches the tag.

findings.claim: [P9] The wait step incorrectly polls the crates.io Web API (`/api/v1/crates/...`), which updates immediately upon publish. Cargo resolves dependencies against the registry index (sparse or git), which updates asynchronously. Polling the Web API will return 200 before the index has actually caught up, failing to prevent the `cargo package` race.
findings.fix: Poll the sparse registry index directly (e.g., `https://index.crates.io/ba/sh/bashrs-oracle`) or use `cargo search bashrs-oracle` to verify the index.

dissent.summary: I have reviewed points 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 from the release diff. Defects were found in P1 (exec_flow method calls bypassing evaluation checks), P2 (array lowering falling through on unsupported stdlib calls), and P8 (publish-from-tag.sh polling the live index during dry runs). Points P6, P7, P9, and P10 were found to be clean.

findings.claim: [P1] is_dynamic_exec only matches Expr::FunctionCall and completely ignores Expr::MethodCall. If a script calls exec or capture as a method (e.g., s.exec()), is_dynamic_exec evaluates to false, leaving dynamic = false. A malicious literal passed to the method bypasses the check_substitution_patterns check and reaches eval unguarded.
findings.fix: Add a match arm in is_dynamic_exec for Expr::MethodCall that checks if name is in EXEC_FNS, and evaluates !is_static_string(receiver) || args.iter().any(|a| !is_static_string(a)).

findings.claim: [P2] convert_array_stdlib_call only intercepts array_len and array_join. Passing a local array to any other function (like __format_concat/println!, or user-defined functions) falls through to convert_expr_to_value, which lowers to the unassigned scalar "$name", crashing under set -u. Furthermore, convert_array_first_arg falls back to "$name" for array parameters.
findings.fix: Apply the array elements reconstruction logic broadly within convert_expr_to_value for any variable known to be an array, rather than intercepting it only for two specific stdlib functions.

findings.claim: [P6] no defect found: SC2046 now correctly reads shell_words::Expansion markers populated by the lexer, and the lexer matches the old scanner's logic exactly (skipping arithmetic expansions, keeping quotes aligned, properly indexing the text).

findings.claim: [P7] no defect found: each dogfood gate accurately measures its target (contracts, corpus JSON fields, README invocations) and exits 1 on any discrepancy, never printing PASS without evaluating the assertions.

While testing on an already-published tag (like v7.0.4) succeeds, a dry run on a *new* unpublished tag will fail when poll_index exhausts its retries, breaking dry-run verifications.
findings.fix: Bypass poll_index when DRY_RUN is set to 1.

findings.claim: [P9] no defect found: the wait step uses a bounded retry loop with curl -f which correctly retries on 404 until success or the 10-attempt limit is reached.
